title: Career Roadmap: Researcher

facts.Current degree: Liberal Arts / Liberal Studies (BA / B.Sc Liberal Arts & Sciences)

blocks.text: A Researcher investigates questions systematically by collecting evidence, analysing information, evaluating existing knowledge, and communicating findings. Researchers working in Politics, Philosophy & Economics (PPE) may explore political institutions, public policy, economic development, ethics, social inequality, governance, and the relationship between markets and society.

A PPE degree is particularly suitable for interdisciplinary research because it combines political analysis, philosophical reasoning, and economic thinking. Graduates can pursue research in universities, think tanks, consulting organisations, public policy institutions, nonprofits, and private-sector research teams.

blocks.label: Qualification note
blocks.text: A bachelor's degree can support entry-level research assistant, project assistant, and junior analyst roles. Independent academic research positions and university faculty careers commonly require postgraduate study and often a PhD. Requirements vary by research field and employer.

items.text: Identify research questions and define the scope of a study.
Review academic papers, books, reports, and existing evidence.
Develop hypotheses, conceptual frameworks, or research propositions.
Collect data through surveys, interviews, archives, public datasets, or experiments where appropriate.
Apply qualitative, quantitative, or mixed research methods.
Analyse findings and assess alternative explanations.
Prepare research reports, literature reviews, policy briefs, and presentations.
Collaborate with faculty members, research teams, or subject specialists.
Maintain accurate citations, research records, and reproducible methods.
Communicate limitations, uncertainty, and implications of the findings.

blocks.text: Political Science Researcher
Studies political institutions, elections, governance, public administration, international relations, and political behaviour.

blocks.label: Skills

Philosophy and Ethics Researcher

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: argument analysis, logic, conceptual reasoning, academic writing
Economics Researcher
Investigates economic growth, inequality, employment, markets, public finance, development, and economic policy.

blocks.label: Skills

Social and Interdisciplinary Researcher

blocks.label: Skills

Recommended subject combinations
The flexible structure of PPE allows students to deepen one discipline while maintaining interdisciplinary understanding.

Students interested in quantitative economics should prioritise mathematics and statistics early. Students targeting philosophy or political theory should focus on logic, argument construction, close reading, and rigorous academic writing.
Core subjects to master

rows.text: Political institutions, political theory, comparative politics, governance
Logic, ethics, epistemology, political philosophy, argument analysis
Research questions, literature reviews, study design, sampling
Descriptive statistics, probability, hypothesis testing, regression
Interviews, case studies, document analysis, thematic coding
Data cleaning, statistical analysis, econometrics where relevant
Argument structure, citations, literature reviews, research reports
Informed consent, confidentiality, attribution, responsible data handling
Presentations, research summaries, seminars, collaborative discussion

blocks.text: Stage 1
Foundations in PPE

items.text: Study introductory political science, philosophy, and economics.
Practise identifying arguments, assumptions, and evidence.
Read introductory academic papers and credible research reports.
Learn academic citation and reference management.
Write short analytical essays on interdisciplinary questions.

blocks.text: Stage 2
Research methods and analytical skills

items.text: Learn research design, literature searches, and source evaluation.
Study statistics and basic data interpretation.
Practise interviews, document analysis, or survey design where appropriate.
Learn Excel and begin using Python or R if quantitative research interests you.
Produce a structured literature review on a focused question.

blocks.text: Stage 3
Specialisation and independent projects

items.text: Select a primary research area within PPE.
Identify a research question with guidance from a faculty mentor.
Collect and analyse suitable evidence.
Compare competing explanations and document limitations.
Present findings through a research paper, poster, or seminar.

blocks.text: Stage 4
Research experience and postgraduate planning

items.text: Apply for research internships and project assistant opportunities.
Develop a portfolio of research papers and analytical projects.
Seek feedback from faculty or experienced researchers.
Prepare an academic CV and a statement of research interests.
Identify master's or doctoral programmes aligned with your chosen field.

blocks.text: Adapt these stages to the duration and curriculum of the selected PPE programme.

rows.text: Google Scholar, university libraries, discipline-specific research databases

blocks.text: Tool selection should follow the research question. Philosophy research may depend primarily on conceptual analysis and textual interpretation, while economics research often needs mathematical and statistical methods.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Comparative governance study
Compare two public institutions or policy approaches using official documents and credible academic literature.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: comparative research, document analysis, evidence synthesis, academic writing

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Ethics and public decision-making
Analyse an ethical dilemma involving fairness, rights, public resources, or emerging technology using clearly defined philosophical frameworks.

blocks.label: Skills

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Economic and social data analysis
Use a public dataset to investigate a question about employment, inequality, education, or economic development.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Interdisciplinary literature review
Review academic literature on a topic such as democracy, inequality, political participation, or technology governance, comparing different disciplinary perspectives.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: literature search, synthesis, source evaluation, research-gap identification

For each project, include the research question, relevant literature, methodology, evidence, analysis, limitations, and conclusion. Distinguish original findings from ideas drawn from existing sources, and cite sources consistently.

By graduation, a strong candidate should aim to have:

items.text: A solid grounding in politics, philosophy, and economics.
A defined research interest and understanding of relevant literature.
Experience with appropriate qualitative or quantitative methods.
Two or three well-documented research projects or writing samples.
Strong analytical writing and presentation skills.
Experience working with a faculty mentor, research team, or internship.
A clear plan for entry-level research employment or postgraduate study.

blocks.label: Final recommendation
blocks.text: PPE is a strong interdisciplinary foundation for research careers, particularly in public policy, political science, philosophy, economics, and social research. Students should use the flexibility of the degree strategically: choose a primary research area, build appropriate methodological skills, complete substantial research projects, and seek mentorship and internships. For long-term independent academic research, plan for postgraduate specialisation and potentially a PhD.
